In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HTLV‐I genome is present in virtually all patients with CTLC, that Tax is expressed in these cells, and that Tax is a potential target for antisense therapy.
HTLV‐I is a cofactor in the pathogenesis and progression of CTCL, but not the cause.
Tax is a marker for the development of CTCL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HTLV‐I is not an etiologic agent for CTCL, but rather that Tax is a transforming protein that may be responsible for the development of the malignant clone in CTCL.
HTLV‐I is not a cause of CTCL but that Tax is an important pathophysiologic component of CTCL.
Tax may play a role in the development of CTCL, but it is not the only factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HTLV‐I infection is associated with the development of CTCL.
HTLV‐I may be involved in the pathogenesis and progression of CTCL in Western patients.
Tax is present in CTCL and may play a significant role in the pathobiology of this disease.
